edges.description: Neomorphic mutant IDH1/IDH2 catalytic activity generates millimolar intratumoral 2-HG that competitively inhibits 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases.
Genome-wide DNA and histone hypermethylation silences lineage-differentiation programs and locks astrocytic precursors in a progenitor-like undifferentiated state.
Tumoral 2-HG release and peritumoral cortical infiltration lower neuronal seizure thresholds and provoke tumor-related epilepsy.
intermediate_mechanisms: Peritumoral cortical neuronal hyperexcitability promoted by extracellular D-2-hydroxyglutarate structural mimicry of glutamate and infiltrative cortical disruption

edges.description: Abrogation of p53-mediated senescence and DNA-damage checkpoints enables sustained clonal proliferation of infiltrative astrocytoma cells.
Loss of functional ATRX/DAXX chromatin remodeling derepresses recombination-mediated telomere elongation (ALT).
Replicative immortality sustained by ALT enables long-term clonal expansion and parenchymal infiltration of astrocytoma cells.
Loss of G1/S cyclin-dependent kinase inhibition accelerates proliferative expansion and malignant progression of infiltrative astrocytoma cells.
edges.source: CDKN2A/B Homozygous Deletion and Cell-Cycle Checkpoint Loss

edges.description: Undifferentiated progenitor-like glioma cells drive continuous proliferation and parenchymal invasion across cerebral cortex and white matter.
Diffuse cortical and subcortical astrocytic infiltration disrupts local excitatory-inhibitory networks and triggers focal or generalized seizures.
Progressive hemispheric tumor volume and peritumoral mass effect elevate intracranial pressure and cause headache.
intermediate_mechanisms: Cerebral parenchymal mass effect, vasogenic edema, and elevated intracranial pressure

edges.description: Diffuse infiltration of frontal and associative cerebral networks impairs memory, attention, and executive cognitive function.
Infiltration and compression of corticospinal motor cortex and subcortical white-matter tracts produce contralateral motor weakness.
Infiltration of dominant-hemisphere perisylvian and frontal language networks produces expressive or receptive aphasia.
